2. Facts in short are that, Sohrab Jan Bhuiyan son of Sarwar Jan Bhuiyan of 333, Elephant Road, P. S. Dhanmondi, District Dhaka, as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 466 of 1979, in the 3rd Court of Munsif. Dhaka, and having been transferred to the 1st Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka, it is renumbered as Title Suit No. 4 of 1984, on the averment that C. S. Plot No. 681 of Mouza Dhanmondi, originally belonged to Ujir Bibi in 16 annas rayati right. Ujir Bibi was the 16 annas owner of entrie C.S. Plot No. 681 measuring 0.33 decimals of land. After the death, of Ujir Bibi her successor in interest and lastly it was transferred to Sufia Begum, mother of the plaintiffs father who thereafter transferred her entrie interest in the plot of the plaintiffs father Mr. Sarwar Jan Bhuiyan by a registered deed of gift dated 20.5.54 and delivered possession to the done. It is the further case that the plaintiffs father purchased the entrie right, title and interest of Abdul Hamid and Syed Abdul Motaleb by two registered deeds of sale dated 22.4.53 and 5.4.53 and thereby got the possession of entire 0.20 decimals of land. His further case is that the plaintiffs father also acquired title and possession in one decimal of land in C. S. Plot No. 680 which was left after requisition for acquisition. When plaintiffs father was in such possession of 0.20 decimals land of C. S. Plot No. 681 and 0.01 decimal of the Plot No. 680 the defendant No. 6 started creating trouble in the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs father by allowing the refuse and polluted water of the staff quarter of the defendant No. 6 to accumulate on the said land and which sometimes used to be over flooded by such refuse and polluted water. The plaintiffs father brought Title Suit No. 146 of 1969 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Dhaka, for permanent injunction restraining the defendant No. 6 from allowing to accumulate the polluted water. The learned Munsif by his judgment dated 21.9.71, after finding title of the plaintiffs father with respect to 0.21 decimals of land of those 2 plots, passed an order of permanent injunction restraining the defendant No. 6 from discharging refuse, polluted and unclean water or any water from the laboratory and the staff quarter of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research upon the suit land. The plaintiff's father put the decree in to execution in Title Execution Case No. 8 of 1972, which is still pending. 

 7. On 11.12.86, the suit was fixed for hearing, but the defendant No. 6 filed an application praying for time, but that was rejected and after examining the witnesses for the plaintiffs the Court decreed the suit ex-parte. 

 8. Against that ex-parte decree the petitioner filed an application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The order dated 24.12.85, decreeing the suit ex-parte was then vacated and the suit was restored to its original file and number by order No. 85 dated 31.8.87 and 8.11.88 was fixed for hearing.
